---
title: "Approximating the Heaviside Step Function with the Hyperbolic Tangent"
author: "Anthony Morciglio"

---

## The Hyperbolic Tangent Function

In this demonstration, we visualize how the **hyperbolic tangent function**  
\[
f(x) = \frac{1}{2}[1 + \tanh(kx)]
\]
approaches the **Heaviside step function** \( H(x) \) as the steepness parameter \( k \) increases.

The parameter \( k \) controls how rapidly the function transitions from 0 to 1:
- For **small** \( k \), the function transitions gradually — forming a smooth "S"-shaped curve.
- For **large** \( k \), the transition becomes nearly vertical around \( x = 0 \), approximating a perfect step.

We will plot \( f(x) \) for several \( k \)-values and compare them to the ideal Heaviside step function.

---

```{r heaviside-tanh, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Define range for x-values
x <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 400)

# Define k-values for comparison
k_values <- c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20)

# Create a data frame with all k-values
data <- expand.grid(x = x, k = k_values) %>%
  mutate(
    tanh_approx = 0.5 * (1 + tanh(k * x)),    # Smoothed Heaviside approximation
    heaviside = ifelse(x < 0, 0, 1)           # True Heaviside step
  )

# Create Custom Blue Pallette
blue_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("#A8D8FF", "#0073CF"))(length(k_values))

# Create the plot
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = tanh_approx, color = factor(k), group = k)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = heaviside), color = "black", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = blue_palette, name = "k-value") +
  labs(
    title = "The Hyperbolic Tangent Function Approaching the Heaviside Step Function",
    subtitle = expression(paste("Comparison of ", (1/2)*(1 + tanh(k*x)), " for various ", k)),
    x = "x",
    y = expression(f(x)),
    caption = "Dashed black line represents the ideal Heaviside step function"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "blue")
  )
```
